source_snapshot.procedure: Login to WebUI KVM and open multiple KVM pages; generic setup/teardown says clear logs and collect photos.
source_snapshot.criteria: The number of KVM sessions must match design; example: if design allows three, three open and a fourth does not.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO correctly identifies the multiple interactive GUI-client boundary but does not distinguish browser tabs from independent backend sessions or define account/scope, input arbitration, limit-plus-one response, existing-session impact or cleanup.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY correctly adds an L and L+1 concurrency matrix and admission outcomes. V3.1 additionally requires unique session IDs, account/role/source dimensions, video continuity, first over-limit evidence and capacity-release proof.

old_problem: Opening several tabs may reuse one authentication or backend KVM session and cannot prove multiple-user capacity. The example count of three is not a universal limit, while the source omits whether the limit is global/per-target/per-account, the L+1 policy, shared/exclusive input behavior, impact on established streams and release after close.
disposition_reason: Parameterize the authoritative concurrent KVM limit as L and bind its scope and session policy from the Project/vendor design. Human operators create distinct authorized backend sessions 1..L and attempt L+1, with visual stream/arbitration evidence, server session/audit IDs and orderly release. The exact L/account matrix is execution configuration rather than an unresolved engineering decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 908, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, adjacent keyboard/mouse case and the preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.
The title, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe design-limited KVM concurrency; the example three/not-four illustrates L/L+1 but does not set L.
Server-side session IDs and distinct authorized client/account context are necessary because tabs or shared cookies can represent one backend session.

ED-08 requires true visual KVM evidence, ED-15 prohibits PASS without the approved design limit/policy, ED-17 preserves audit logs and ED-20 keeps concurrent capacity separate from single-session input fidelity.

test_case.test_name: Manually verify KVM concurrent-session limit L, L+1 policy and capacity release
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC remote-KVM server admits distinct authorized sessions through the Project-approved limit L for the same verified target, preserves existing streams and the specified view/input ownership policy, handles one additional session exactly as designed and releases capacity after orderly or defined abnormal closure.
required_package: BMC/SUT identity, BMC/KVM firmware, supported client/browser/plugin/OS/network-path versions and safe visual test surface
Authoritative L and whether it is global, per BMC, per SUT, per account, per role, per source IP or another scope
Distinct authorized account/role/client/source-IP matrix and requirement for unique authenticated backend session IDs
Expected outcomes for sessions 1..L and L+1: admit, reject, queue, view-only, takeover, preempt or other defined state
Shared/exclusive input ownership, safe marker, prohibited actions, video independence, latency and established-session impact limits
Idle/session timeout, logout and approved abnormal-close behavior plus maximum capacity-release time
Timestamped visual recording, KVM session table, BMC audit and per-client console/network evidence plan
test_case.test_command: MANUAL ONLY. Preserve audit/session/browser/host logs. Verify every client points to the same approved BMC/SUT but uses the Project-required distinct account/client/session context; multiple tabs sharing a token do not count. Open sessions sequentially from 1 through L, recording backend session ID, identity, admission, video continuity and the specified input ownership using only a nominated operator and safe marker. Attempt exactly one L+1 session and preserve the first reject/queue/view-only/takeover/preemption result and its effect on every existing session; do not repeatedly retry. Close sessions in the approved order, including the defined abnormal-close checkpoint if in scope, and prove locks/capacity/audit state recover within the limit without rebooting BMC or DUT.
test_case.expected_result: Sessions 1..L are distinct backend sessions and are admitted with the designed view/input policy, correct target video and acceptable impact on earlier sessions. Session L+1 receives exactly the specified over-limit outcome without unapproved access, console corruption or loss of established sessions. Closing clients releases capacity and leaves no orphaned session/lock within the approved time. The example value three is used only if Project SPEC sets L=3.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative L/scope/policy, unique server-side evidence for 1..L and L+1, visual continuity/arbitration checks for every admitted session, first-attempt over-limit behavior and verified cleanup/capacity release with engineer/operator sign-off. Tabs, shared tokens, login count, screenshots without session IDs or testing only L cannot pass. Wrong target, unauthorized admission, incorrect reject/queue/takeover, unaccepted impact/preemption, uncontrolled input, orphaned session or release timeout is FAIL. Missing L, scope, client/account matrix or policy is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Preserve BMC audit, KVM session, browser/client and host logs; do not clear concurrency evidence.
Use only authorized accounts and prove distinct backend sessions; do not share credentials or bypass RBAC/session security.
Verify all clients target the same approved SUT and nominate one safe input owner; prohibit simultaneous uncontrolled input, power/reset, BIOS/firmware, destructive shell and credential actions.
Attempt L+1 once and preserve the first response; do not reconnect repeatedly or disrupt accepted sessions to force a result.
Close every session and verify release without rebooting BMC/DUT; stop on wrong target, unexpected takeover/preemption, lost console or unintended input.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/KVM/client versions and authoritative L/scope/policy with account-role-source-client matrix
For sessions 1..L and L+1: unique backend session ID, account/role/source, timestamps, admission state and redacted KVM visual evidence
Existing-session video continuity, latency/disconnect and safe view/input ownership/arbitration evidence at every admission and L+1 attempt
BMC KVM session table/audit logs plus client console/network records proving first over-limit behavior without retry
Ordered logout/close and approved abnormal-close checkpoint with capacity/lock/audit release proof
No credential/policy/power/log mutation, explicit untested combinations, unchanged SUT and manual engineer/operator verdict
test_case.recovery: If a session targets the wrong SUT, gains unexpected input control or preempts/corrupts an existing session, stop all input and close the offending client according to the approved session runbook. Preserve first-failure evidence, verify SUT state independently and have the BMC owner release any orphaned session without reboot/power action unless separately authorized. Do not automatically reconnect or repeat L+1.

source_conflict.reason: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently target design-specific concurrent KVM capacity. The exact limit and scope are Project parameters, not contradictory semantics.

blocked.reason: The L/L+1 manual method, evidence and safety boundaries are complete. Project capacity/session policy and authorized clients can make execution ready.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Authoritative L and scope, client/account/role/source matrix, admission and L+1 policy, view/input arbitration, video/latency impact limits, timeout/close/release behavior and evidence ownership.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; MULTIPLE AUTHORIZED MANUAL GUI CLIENTS REQUIRED; NO UNCONTROLLED INPUT, CREDENTIAL SHARING, POWER/RESET OR RETRY

project_authority: Project BMC/KVM capacity and security specification, vendor remote-console/session manual, RBAC policy and audit/session schema define L, scope, arbitration and release acceptance.
